body:
A data point from a different case: one GPU, with big MXFP4 expert blobs and most of them on the CPU lane. **Here `DS4_RING_MB=128` makes long prompts ~10% slower.** So we'd size the ring in slots (blob size), not in MB.

**Why it differs from yours:** our experts are DeepSeek's MXFP4 (unsloth's UD-Q8_K_XL), ~19.4 MB a blob against your ~8.8 MB. With the code in `ds4_model.cu:4287-4292`, 400 MiB is 20 slots (5 a batch), but 128 MiB is only 4, the `kParts` minimum, one slot a batch. Yours kept 16.

**Measured** (1× L40S 48 GB, Xeon Platinum 8580 VM with 32 vCPUs, ~504 GB RAM, Maya v1.1.34, `--tp 2 --threads on --cpu-threads 28 --mmap-experts off --dspark on`, 262K context; ~91% of the experts on the CPU lane). Four starts in the order A B A B, page cache dropped before each; fresh prompts, prompt tok/s from the server's timings:

| `DS4_RING_MB` | Experts in VRAM | 10.4K | 42.8K | 174K | 42.8K, second prompt | Decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 (default) | 1,357 | 563 / 710 | 1,214 / 1,412 | **1,893 / 1,952** | **1,436 / 1,458** | 40.9 / 41.0 |
| 128 | 1,373 | 633 / 636 | 1,229 / 1,232 | **1,705 / 1,711** | **1,304 / 1,315** | 41.6 / 41.7 |

- **Long prompts:** 128 is ~10% slower at 174K and on the second 42.8K prompt, in both pairs.
- **Short prompts:** within our run-to-run spread at 10.4K and the first 42.8K. The 400 starts vary more (563-710); 128 is steadier, but not faster on average.
- **Decode:** the freed VRAM buys 16 more experts here (yours bought ~33 a card, since your blobs are half the size), worth ~1.5%.

So on your question: sizing by link speed might explain your slow Gen2 x4 card. Sizing by blob size would avoid our case, where 128 MiB drops the ring to one slot a batch. Something like "N slots a batch" (yours: 4 a batch at 128 MiB) rather than a fixed MB could get you your gain without costing big-blob packs theirs.

Thanks - that pins the unit down. Confirming your reading of the code on v1.1.35 (`ds4_model.cu:4287-4292`):
`ring_n = max(kParts, ((mb << 20) / stride) / kParts * kParts)` with `kParts = 4` and `stride` = the device's
largest trunk-layer expert blob. One correction to my numbers above: on the GSQ-RCO pack the largest blob is
8.97 MiB (CUDA0's layers) / 9.76 MiB (CUDA1's), so 128 MiB is 12 slots = 3 a batch here, not 16 / 4.

### The slot curve on this rig

Same setup as the issue (2x CMP 170HX 64 GB, card 1 on PCIe Gen2 x4 at 1.63 GB/s measured, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
GSQ-RCO IQ2_XXS, layer split, ~2200 experts on the CPU lane), one binary, one run each except 128 and 72 MiB,
which ran twice. Fresh prompts:
our 8K prefill plus the community suite's 4K / 16K / 32K, prompt tok/s.

| `DS4_RING_MB` | slots a batch (CUDA0 / CUDA1) | 8K | 4K | 16K | 32K | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 (default) | 11 / 10 | 694.7 | 1036.8 | 1609.7 | 1756.1 | 52.0 |
| 280 | 7 / 7 | 721.6 | 1106.7 | 1641.9 | 1774.1 | 53.7 |
| 128 | 3 / 3 | 738.1 | 1187.3 | 1727.5 | 1860.0 | 53.2 |
| 72 | 2 / **1 (the floor)** | 753.9 | 1206.5 | 1755.4 | 1881.2 | 52.9 |

The repeats: 128 MiB 724.9 / 1189.4 / 1746.0 / 1876.4 and 72 MiB 725.3 / 1205.8 / 1764.9 / 1886.4 (8K / 4K / 16K /
32K) - 72 MiB stays 0.5-1.6 % ahead of 128 on prompts across both pairs and 0.6-1.3 % behind on decode, inside our
spread at the long end. Experts in VRAM move very little across the sweep (CUDA1: 6731 at 400 MiB -> 6771 at 72, of
7680 a card), so the prompt gain is not the freed VRAM; and decode shows no trend (52.0-53.7).

So the two rigs sit at opposite ends: yours (one fast-link card, 19.4 MB blobs, ~91 % streamed) wants ~5 a batch
and loses ~10 % at 1; this one (the second card on Gen2 x4, ~9 MB blobs, ~14 % streamed) keeps gaining down to
1 a batch on the slow card (+16 % at 4K, +7 % at 32K against the default). I have not isolated why - smaller
batches presumably let a layer's first experts compute while the slow link is still delivering the rest, where on
a fast link the same small batch only serializes copy against compute. That part is a guess.

Either way MB is the wrong unit for the setting: the default 400 lands at 1 a batch on a hypothetical 25 MB-blob
pack and at 11 here. Sizing in slots a batch, as you suggest, with the MB derived from the stride, would make the
default mean the same thing on every pack; something like 4 a batch (16 slots) would be ~140-155 MiB on this pack
and ~310 MiB on yours - close to both measured good regions (this rig gains only 1-2 % more below 3 a batch).

Two more points, on v1.1.36 (same box and pack as my table above; one start each, page cache dropped before each), in case they help size the ring in slots. Slots from `ring_n = max(4, (mb<<20) / stride / 4 * 4)` with our 18,800,640 B blobs:

| `DS4_RING_MB` | Slots (a batch) | Experts in VRAM | 10.4K | 42.7K | 174K | Decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 (default) | 20 (5) | 1,357 | 712 | 1,420 | **1,965** | 40.4 |
| 310 | 16 (4) | 1,361 | 612 | 1,279 | 1,881 | 40.9 |
| 233 | 12 (3) | 1,365 | 693 | 1,368 | 1,893 | 41.3 |
| 128 (v1.1.34, from above) | 4 (1) | 1,373 | 633-636 | 1,229-1,232 | 1,705-1,711 | 41.6 |

On this pack, every ring below the default reads long prompts slower (-4% at 174K with 3-4 a batch, -13% with 1), while decode gains only 1-3% from the 4-16 extra experts. Short prompts are noisy here (the 400 starts ranged 563-712 at 10.4K). So a fixed slot count wouldn't settle it either: 4 a batch is about what you gained with, and it costs us ~4%. The link and the CPU lane seem to matter as much as the blob size, so maybe it could be measured at start, as `lane-times.txt` is.

Thank you, and thanks to everyone who measured in this thread - the slot-based reading was right. In v1.1.39 the prompt ring is no longer a fixed 400 MB: at load the engine measures each GPU's host link (a few ms) and sizes the ring to about 10 ms of that link a batch, at least one expert, at most the old 400 MB and at most 1/16 of the GPU's room for experts. A slow link like yours gets a small ring; a fast one keeps 400 MB (on our V100 the new default picks the same ring as before, which was the fastest we tried there). The log's "prompt ring" line shows the choice, and `DS4_RING_MB` (a size, or `auto`) still sets it. A run on your cards with the default would be welcome.

Released in **v1.1.39**: https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/releases/tag/v1.1.39

Thanks. We ran the v1.1.39 default on the same rig (2x CMP 170HX 64 GB, sm_80, card 0 PCIe Gen2 x16, card 1 Gen2 x4; GSQ-RCO IQ2_XXS pack, `--dspark on`, 512K context). It picks:

```
ds4: CUDA0 prompt ring: 24 slots of 9.0 MB, 6 a batch (215 MB) for its 6.2 GB/s link (DS4_RING_MB sets it)
ds4: CUDA1 prompt ring: 4 slots of 9.8 MB, 1 a batch (39 MB) for its 1.6 GB/s link (DS4_RING_MB sets it)
```

Against `DS4_RING_MB=128`, same binary, two repeats each, the default was slower: Strata 4K / 16K / 32K prompts -2.9 / -3.5 / -3.4 %, and decode **-10 %** (`--dspark on`) or **-20 %** (`--dspark none`).

**The decode loss is not the ring. It is the link measurement.** With `--dspark none` (decode tok/s, 5x512, temp 0):

| setup | decode |
|---|---:|
| `DS4_RING_MB=128` | 43.3 |
| fixed 39 MB, 215 MB; per card 24 / 4 slots set directly (test knob, no measurement) | 43.1-43.4 |
| `DS4_RING_MB=128` + `link_h2d()` called anyway, result unused | **34.8** (text identical to the 128 run) |

We then split `link_h2d()` into its steps, ring fixed at 128 MB:

| what runs at load | decode |
|---|---:|
| nothing | 43.0 |
| all of `link_h2d()` | 35.2 |
| the host/device allocations, stream, events - no copies | 43.2 |
| only the pinned host alloc + memset / only the `cudaMalloc` | 43.0 / 43.4 |
| all of it without the closing `cudaGetLastError()` | 34.5 |
| all of it, but the four copies and events on the legacy stream (`0`) instead of the new non-blocking one | 42.8 (it measures the same 6.18 / 1.63 GB/s) |

All seven runs produced the same five texts. So the timed copies on a fresh non-blocking stream leave decode ~20 % slower for the rest of the run, though the stream is destroyed right after. While decoding in the slow runs, card 0's SM load drops (42 vs 50 %) and host DRAM traffic rises (3.5 vs 2.3 GB/s). We don't know the mechanism.

The tables above are from our fork (v1.1.39 merged with our patches). Stock v1.1.39, upstream env only, `--dspark none`, two repeats: 128 MB 39.5 / 39.1 tok/s, the default 31.7 / 31.2. The same 20 %.

A possible fix, the one we tested (row 6): time the copies on the legacy stream.

```diff
-                if (cudaEventRecord(e0, s) != cudaSuccess || cudaMemcpyAsync(v, h, nb, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, s) != cudaSuccess ||
-                    cudaEventRecord(e1, s) != cudaSuccess || cudaEventSynchronize(e1) != cudaSuccess ||
+                if (cudaEventRecord(e0, 0) != cudaSuccess || cudaMemcpyAsync(v, h, nb, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, 0) != cudaSuccess ||
+                    cudaEventRecord(e1, 0) != cudaSuccess || cudaEventSynchronize(e1) != cudaSuccess ||
```

**On the size:** here the best prompt ring is the smallest. With `--dspark none`, fixed 39 MB (4 slots a card, 1 a batch) read 4K / 16K / 32K at 987 / 1396 / 1600 tok/s, against 941 / 1379 / 1580 for 128 MB and 915 / 1357 / 1563 for 215 MB. Per card 24 / 4 slots read 954 / 1368 / 1571, 4 / 24 slots 955 / 1400 / 1607, so card 0's larger ring costs the long prompts most. One run with DSpark on agrees (39 MB: 4K +1.9 %, 16K +1.2 %, decode the same as 128 MB); repeats are running. So on this x16 Gen2 card, about 10 ms of link a batch is more than it needs. One expert a batch reads fastest on both cards.

Thank you - this was a great piece of work. You found the decode loss, showed it was the link measurement and not the ring, split `link_h2d()` into its steps until only the timed copies on the new stream were left, and tested the fix. That saved us a lot of time.

**Fixed in v1.1.42** (in the way you suggested): the four timed copies and their events now run on the legacy stream, as the ordinary load copies do. No stream is made for the measurement any more. The ring sizes stay the same, since it measures the same bandwidth (your row 6: 6.18 / 1.63 GB/s).

We could not reproduce the loss on our own machines. On a V100 (PCIe 3 x16, a CPU-heavy decode) runs with the same text decoded the same, within noise, with the old fresh-stream measurement, the legacy-stream one, or none. A small probe on an RTX 3050 also showed no lasting effect on later streams or copy engines. So we don't know the mechanism either. Our guess is something in how the driver hands out hardware queues or copy engines on your GA100 cards, but we have not confirmed it. Your row 6 is the evidence for this fix. The ring choice on our V100 is unchanged: 60 slots, 396 MB, 12.3 GB/s.

**The ring size:** your numbers convinced us. On your x16 Gen2 card one expert takes about 1.5 ms on the link, and one expert a batch read 4K-32K prompts 2-3.5% faster than the 6 of the ~10 ms rule. Our V100s and the L40S, where an expert takes 0.5-0.8 ms on the link, were fastest with the big ring. So the rule now reads: where one expert takes 1 ms or more on the link, a batch is one expert; otherwise about 10 ms of the link, as before. On your rig both cards then get 4 slots (one a batch). Our V100s pick the same ring as before. `DS4_RING_MB` still overrides it.

Could you check two things on v1.1.42?
1. With the new binary and no `DS4_RING_MB`: decode with `--dspark none` should be back at your 128 MB numbers (~39-43 tok/s), and the log should show `CUDA0 prompt ring: 4 slots ... 1 a batch` and the same for CUDA1.
2. 4K / 16K / 32K prompt speed against `DS4_RING_MB=39`: they should be the same, within noise.

Released in **v1.1.42**: https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/releases/tag/v1.1.42

Thanks for the fix. Both checks pass on v1.1.42.

Setup as in my v1.1.39 report: stock v1.1.42 build (no patches of ours, upstream env only), the same rig (2x CMP 170HX, card0 Gen2 x16, card1 Gen2 x4) and the same config, two repeats per arm.

**1. Decode with `--dspark none`, no `DS4_RING_MB`.** It is back at the 128 MB numbers:

| ring | decode tok/s (2 runs) | 8K prompt tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| link-sized default (v1.1.42) | 39.8 / 39.7 | 638.8 / 633.8 |
| `DS4_RING_MB=128` | 39.7 / 39.7 | 621.1 / 625.1 |
| for comparison, v1.1.39 default | 31.7 / 31.2 | 563.1 / 562.9 |
| for comparison, v1.1.39 128 MB | 39.5 / 39.1 | 561.4 / 552.2 |

The log shows the rule you described:

```
ds4: CUDA0 prompt ring: 4 slots of 9.0 MB, 1 a batch (36 MB) for its 6.2 GB/s link (DS4_RING_MB sets it)
ds4: CUDA1 prompt ring: 4 slots of 9.8 MB, 1 a batch (39 MB) for its 1.6 GB/s link (DS4_RING_MB sets it)
```

**2. 4K / 16K / 32K prompts, default vs `DS4_RING_MB=39`** (Strata suite medians, DSpark on). They are the same within noise, under 0.5 % apart:

| ring | 4K | 16K | 32K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| link-sized default | 933.9 / 929.1 | 1640.9 / 1638.7 | 1793.6 / 1793.8 |
| `DS4_RING_MB=39` | 931.8 / 930.1 | 1633.3 / 1639.4 | 1793.2 / 1792.3 |

Decode with DSpark was 46.7 / 46.8 vs 46.5 / 46.9 tok/s, and the decoded texts were identical between the two rings. That fits both now streaming one expert a batch. So we can drop `DS4_RING_MB` from our config.
